s_open.name: 15:00, Wednesday
s_open.title: 15:00, Wednesday
s_open.body:
You are covering a shift for Danni, who called in sick.

Rachel, 24. She works Wednesdays at a garden centre on the north side of town. The roster says collect her at 3:00 and drive her to physio at 3:30.

You have never met her. Her photo is on her profile, so you know who you are looking for. You are parked where you can see the front doors.

It is three o'clock. The only thing you have is last week's note.

s_note.name: The note
s_note.title: Last Wednesday's note
s_note.body:
Took Rachel to work. All good. She seemed a little tired in the car.

That is the whole note. Eleven words.

q_arrive.name: She doesn't come out
q_arrive.title: Nobody comes out
q_arrive.body:
Ten past three. Staff come and go through the front doors. None of them is Rachel.

Physio is a twelve minute drive and they give fifteen minutes' grace. Your next client is at four, across town.

What do you do?

choices.label: Give her a few more minutes
Go inside and ask for her
Log it as a no-show and get to your next client

s_wait.name: You wait
s_wait.title: You give her a few more minutes
s_wait.body:
Half past three. You get out and walk to the front doors.

Rachel is round the back, sitting on a pallet by the loading door. She has been there since three.

She does not wait out the front. She stacks shelves in the back and she likes it that way — she would rather the town did not watch her being collected every Wednesday.

You leave at 3:22. Physio's fifteen minutes are gone.

s_inside.name: You go inside
s_inside.title: You go inside and ask
s_inside.body:
A supervisor points you round the back without looking up. "She'll be by the loading door. She's always there."

Rachel is on a pallet by the roller door with her bag on her knees. She has been there since three.

She works in the back. She prefers it. And she would rather not be collected in front of the whole car park every week.

You make physio with two minutes to spare.

s_office.name: You ring the office
s_office.title: You ring the office
s_office.body:
Someone answers and opens the file while you wait. The note says what you have already read.

"She should be out the front," they say — because that is what the roster says, and the roster is all they have too.

They ring the garden centre. At 3:16 they ring you back: she is round the back by the loading door, and apparently she always is.

You miss the grace period by four minutes.

s_noshow.name: You log a no-show
s_noshow.title: You log it as a no-show
s_noshow.body:
It is the defensible call. You waited, she did not come out, and you have a client at four.

You tap client not present and drive across town.

Rachel sat on the pallet until twenty to four. Then she walked home, because she did not have anyone's number and the office had already gone quiet for the afternoon.

She was there the whole time.

The file now says she was not. At her next plan review, that is one more line saying this support is not being used.

q_note.name: Your turn to write
q_note.title: You are writing your own note now
q_note.body:
Next Wednesday somebody covers Rachel. It might be Danni. It might be someone who has never met her.

Which of these would you write?

choices.label: "Collected Rachel from work and drove her to physio. All went well."
choices.feedback: "All went well" is your judgement, and the next worker cannot act on it. They will stand at the front doors exactly like you did.

choices.label: "Rachel finishes in the back and waits by the loading door, not the front entrance. She'd rather not be collected where the whole car park can see. Collected her at 3:10 and drove her to physio."
choices.feedback: This is the one — and the second sentence is the important half. Where she waits is useful. Why she waits there stops the next worker deciding the front would be easier.

choices.label: "Rachel wasn't waiting where she was supposed to be."
choices.feedback: "Supposed to be" makes it Rachel's error. She was exactly where she always is. The only thing that was not where it should have been is the information.

s_end.name: Debrief
s_end.title: Nothing went wrong except the note
s_end.body:
The roster was right. You were on time. Rachel finished when she always finishes and waited where she always waits.

There was no mix-up to untangle. There was one fact, and it was not written down.

Danni never wrote it because Danni just goes round the back. After a few months it stopped being a thing you would think to mention — it was simply how the shift went.

That is the whole trap. The things you learn about someone stop feeling like information once you know them. They feel like the job.

They are not the job. They are the part of the job that leaves with you.

Here is the note that would have prevented all of it:

Drove Rachel to the garden centre for her 9:00 start. She works in the back and waits by the loading door when she finishes, not the front entrance — she would rather not be collected where the whole car park can see. Collected her at 3:05 and drove her to physio.

Twenty-eight words. About a minute.

A note is not for you. It is for the day you are not there.
